title.narrative: Improving the Science, Technology, Engineering, and Mathematics Secondary Education Project

description.narrative: The project aims to build a human capital base to support Tajikistan's transition to higher labor productivity and competitiveness. It will strengthen gender-inclusive access to quality secondary education in science, technology, engineering, and mathematics (STEM) subjects and develop climate change awareness among the country's secondary school graduates. The project proposes to modernize teaching, upgrade the learning environment, improve school management, introduce and integrate climate change education, and expand girls' participation in STEM studies and women's career paths toward high-productivity sectors.

description.narrative: Learning outcome of secondary education students on STEM subjects and their preparedness for tackling climate change impacts improved

42% of grade 9 completers (43% F) reached at least basic level of competency in applying sciences and mathematics knowledge to ‘real world' situations Progress/Status: The first round of assessment will be done in Q1 2029 Data Source: Survey on applying sciences and mathematics knowledge to ‘real world' situations Baseline value: Less than 40%

At least 1 percentage point increase in the proportion of grade 11 completers (at least 0.5 percentage point higher for girls) registered in Cluster 1 in the national tests Progress/Status: The first tracer study will be done in 2026 Data Source: Annual project progress report by the project administration group, National Testing Center report Baseline value: 11.1%

At least 50% of grade 9 female completers assessed at school with IT competency and are aware of basic climate change resilience practices Progress/Status: The first round of assessment will be done in Q1 2029 Data Source: Surveys on students' IT competency and their understanding of climate change Baseline value: 42.9%
Output/s as listed by the project staff.

Output: Climate change education and disaster resilience capacity enhanced Indicator: 450 teachers and teacher trainers (45% F) on STEM trained on climate change (2023 baseline: NA, 39.1% of STEM teachers are F) (OP 2.1.1, OP 3.2.2) Progress/Status: Under development and to be continued in Q4 2025.
As of December 2025. Under development and to be continued. Data Source: Quarterly project progress report by PAG Actual value:

Output: Climate change education and disaster resilience capacity enhanced Indicator: 5 representative schools* (4 in rural areas), reconstructed and/or provided with STEM blocks and sex-segregated WASH facilities compliant with climate change risk and disaster risk resilience including seismic proofing requirements (2023 Baseline: these school facilities not climate and disaster risk-resilient) (OP 2.4.1, OP 3.2.5) Progress/Status: Under the CW01 procurement package, the design and estimate documentation has been completed for 4 target schools. Currently, the tender process for selecting a construction company for 4 schools is ongoing.
As of December 2025. The preparation of detailed design and cost estimate documentation for the construction of additional STEM blocks in 20 target schools has been fully completed and approved by the State Expertise. At the same time, the procurement processes for the selection of construction companies were initiated and implemented. Currently, under the civil works component of the project, the procurement processes have been completed and contracts have been signed with the winning construction companies as follows: CW01: Contracts were signed on 20 November 2025 with LLC “Dashti Gulho” and LLC “Faridun”. CW02: Contracts were signed on 15 December 2025 with the following winning companies by lot: Lot 1: LLC Fido Sokhtmon Lot 2: LLC Tillo Khan Lot 3: LLC Fido Sokhtmon CW06: Contracts were signed on 24 December 2025 with the following winning companies by lot: Lot 1: LLC Hokimi Chorbog Lot 2: LLC Sangrezi Kulob Lot 3: LLC Hokimi Chorbog Data Source: Quarterly project progress report by PAG Actual value:

Output: Climate change education and disaster resilience capacity enhanced Indicator: 80 community awareness-raising events on climate change held (50% audience are F) (2023 Baseline: NA; 49.7% population are F) (OP 2.5.1, OP 3.2.2) Progress/Status: The selection process for procurement package CS08, carried out in close coordination with ADB, has been fully completed. As a result, a contract was signed with LLC “Alomat” on 5 September 2025. The firm has commenced its activities and is currently in the process of preparing its Inception Report.
As of December 2025. To support the implementation of community awareness-raising activities on climate change, an international consultant conducted a training on climate change issues for selected representatives of the MoES, the TSPU and a Pedagogical college. The training strengthened participants' capacity to deliver climate change awareness activities at the community level, with a focus on gender-responsive approaches. Data Source: Survey of participants' satisfaction Actual value:

Output: Climate change education and disaster resilience capacity enhanced Indicator: At least 5 gender-responsive climate change modules developed and provided for updating curricula, and adopted in TLMs and in the pilot pre-service teacher education program (2023 Baseline: NA) Progress/Status: Developing of 5 gender-responsive climate change modules will be done by CS03 in collaboration with PISF team.
As of December 2025. Developing of 5 gender-responsive climate change modules will be done by CS03 in collaboration with PISF team. Data Source: (i) Clearance by the Research Center under the Academy of Education, and approval by MOES; (ii) endorsement by the RTMC, clearance by the Higher Education Department, and approval by MOES; and (iii) quarterly project progress report by PAG Actual value:

Output: Learning environment improved Indicator: 15 selected schools, including 14 in rural areas, provided with climate risk and disaster risk-resilient and energy-efficient STEM blocks and classrooms, and sex-segregated WASH facilities (2023 Baseline: these schools need emergency repair or reconstruction, and lack WASH facilities) Progress/Status: Works under Procurement Package CW01 are progressing in accordance with the planned schedule. Currently, the tender process for selecting a construction company is ongoing for the construction of secondary schools No.35 in Vahdat, No.4 in Danghara, No.3 in Mu'minobod, and No.8 in Kulob. The submission of applications is still open, with the final deadline set for the end of October 2025. In addition, within the same procurement package, the design and cost estimate documents for schools No.16 in Kaftarkhona village, No.19 in Hamadoni district, and No.67 in Danghara district have been finalized and submitted to the State Expertise Authority for review. The preparation of an updated Environmental Impact Assessment (EIA) was initiated. This report focuses on the construction and rehabilitation of climate risk and disaster risk-resilient, energy-efficient STEM blocks and classrooms, along with sex-segregated WASH facilities. The EIA aims to assess the potential impacts of the project on the environment and society and propose robust mitigation measures. The report was developed based on field surveys, analysis of existing conditions.
As of December 2025. The preparation of detailed design and cost estimate documentation for the construction of additional STEM blocks in 20 target schools has been fully completed and approved by the State Expertise. At the same time, the procurement processes for the selection of construction companies were initiated and implemented. Currently, under the civil works component of the project, the procurement processes have been completed and contracts have been signed with the winning construction companies as follows: CW01: Contracts were signed on 20 November 2025 with LLC “Dashti Gulho” and LLC “Faridun”. CW02: Contracts were signed on 15 December 2025 with the following winning companies by lot: Lot 1: LLC Fido Sokhtmon Lot 2: LLC Tillo Khan Lot 3: LLC Fido Sokhtmon CW06: Contracts were signed on 24 December 2025 with the following winning companies by lot: Lot 1: LLC Hokimi Chorbog Lot 2: LLC Sangrezi Kulob Lot 3: LLC Hokimi Chorbog Data Source: Quarterly project progress report by PAG Actual value:

Output: Learning environment improved Indicator: 20 selected schools, including 18 in rural areas, equipped with modern science laboratories and ICT facilities backed up with stable electricity solutions and installed with heat pumps (2023 Baseline: these schools lack science laboratories and ICT facilities, run power outages, and lack clean heating) Progress/Status: The specifications for the laboratory equipment are now under review and discussion.
As of December 2025. The specifications for the laboratory equipment are now under review and discussion. Data Source: Quarterly project progress report by PAG Actual value:

Output: Quality of STEM education improved Indicator: 450 in-service STEM teachers and teacher trainers (45% F) trained on skills-based approach, STEM subjects and/or cross-subjects, using laboratory practical application (2023 Baseline: no such training systematically, 39.1% of 386 in-service STEM teachers are F) Progress/Status: As of December 2025. HRDT plan discussed, drafted and submitted. Implementation is planned for a later period. Teacher training on using educational technology facilities will start in 2026. Data Source: Quarterly project progress report by PAG Actual value:

Output: Quality of STEM education improved Indicator: Gender-responsive TLMs on grades 5 to 11 STEM subjects updated in line with skills-based approach, and 20 digital libraries on STEM subjects, available for all STEM teachers and students in project schools (2023 Baseline: TLMs outdated and not available for all teachers and students, no digital library) Progress/Status: As of December 2025. The PISF team has developed Guidelines for Preparing STEM TLMs for Grades 5-11. The Guidelines were prepared in two languages (English and Russian) and are currently under review for approval by the MoES. In addition, the first capacity-building seminar for PISF consultants on the development of skills-based TLMs was organized and conducted, laying the foundation for a unified methodological approach. Starting from the first quarter of 2026, PISF will enter the active phase of TLM development.
Data Source: Quarterly project progress report by PAG Actual value:

Output: Climate change education and disaster resilience capacity enhanced Indicator: Detailed model designs of general secondary school buildings on climate change risk and disaster risk resilience including seismic proofing developed and endorsed (2023 Baseline: national building codes have seismic proofing but no climate change risk or other disaster risk resilience requirements) (OP 3.2.5) Progress/Status: The development of detailed model designs for general secondary school buildings incorporating climate change risk and disaster resilience, including seismic proofing, has been completed for 7 target schools. The preparation of an updated Environmental Impact Assessment (EIA) was initiated. This report focuses on the construction and rehabilitation of climate risk and disaster risk-resilient, energy-efficient STEM blocks and classrooms, along with sex-segregated WASH facilities. The EIA aims to assess the potential impacts of the project on the environment and society and propose robust mitigation measures. The report was developed based on field surveys, analysis of existing conditions.
As of December 2025. Detailed model designs of general secondary school buildings addressing climate change risk and disaster risk resilience, including seismic proofing, have been developed and endorsed for 20 target schools. Data Source: Approval by the MOES Baseline year: 2023 Baseline value: N Baseline year: 2023 Baseline value: N Target year: 2029 Target value: Y

Output: Female-friendly STEM education system promoted Indicator: 16 new labs and learning spaces reconstructed or built, 2 WASH facilities built and 2 female dormitory buildings at TSPU and DPC renovated (2023 Baseline: labs inadequate and outdated for STEM, lack of WASH facilities and dormitories in need of repair) Progress/Status: Expected to start in Q1 2026.
As of December 2025. Expected to start in Q1 2026. Data Source: Quarterly project progress report by PAG; GAP monitoring Baseline year: 2023 Baseline value: N Baseline year: 2023 Baseline value: N Target year: 2029 Target value: Y

Output: Female-friendly STEM education system promoted Indicator: 600 female STEM teacher candidates newly enrolled in TSPU and DPC received scholarships, 600 schoolgirls from grades 9-11 at the project schools received stipends, and 50 in-service female STEM teachers at the project schools received research assistantships (2023 Baseline: No scholarship specialized on STEM, no such stipends or assistantships) Progress/Status: The Gender Operational Manual developed and currently on MoES approval. The manual outlines the complete stipend payment process for school students, university students, and teachers, as well as procedures for awarding research grants. It incorporates a gender-sensitive approach, defines criteria for different target groups, and details payment mechanisms and monitoring processes. Starting in October, a call for applications is planned, along with the collection and evaluation of supporting documents from applicants.
As of December 2025. The Gender Operational Manual and the Regulation on the Scholarship and Incentive Program have been developed. The Gender Operational Manual is currently under review by MoES, while the Regulation was approved by MoES on 17 December 2025. The Regulation outlines all mechanisms and rules for providing stipends and incentives, including the complete stipend payment process for school students, university students, and teachers. A series of meetings were conducted in target schools, TSPU, and DPC with students, university students, teachers, and parents to raise awareness about the programs. Data Source: Quarterly project progress report by PAG; GAP monitoring Baseline year: 2023 Baseline value: N Baseline year: 2023 Baseline value: N Target year: 2029 Target value: Y

This package will support the development and delivery of reproductive health and rights courses for 2,000 female secondary school students (Grades 9-11). Data Source: Endorsement by the RTMC and approval by MOES; Quarterly project progress report by PAG; GAP monitoring Baseline year: 2023 Baseline value: N Baseline year: 2023 Baseline value: N Target year: 2029 Target value: Y
